correctness.rationale: Parity-degree 5 bounds force at least four guards of each parity. Direct weight-one/three/five neighborhood reasoning classifies every eligible parity four-set as one of 40 affine two-plane cosets. Independence of the two parity choices yields exactly 1600 total optima. Their three-point intersection obstruction proves zero exchanges. The finite stabilizer calculation partitions 40 opposite-parity choices into 1+3+12+12+12 and exact perfect-matching checks show four paired strata; this yields 1120 paired optima. The standalone packaged Python verifier checks 1820 4-subsets per parity, all 3840 graph symmetries, 48 stabilizer maps, perfect matching by permutation, zero exchanges, and all 10,518,300 8-subsets; it completed successfully.

value.rationale: Five-cube guard deployment with an adjacent backup match is a natural finite optimization problem at the smallest five-dimensional nontrivial case: the previously known optimum cardinality does not reveal that 480 of 1600 minimum total solutions fail the matching condition, that the others fall into four matching orbits, or that every optimum total and paired configuration is frozen under one-token exchanges. The exact orbit decomposition is a complete structural classification, not an arbitrary partial enumeration; it is relevant to robustness of optimal deployment under one-at-a-time changes.
